text:
mike: Heads up — we've got recurring p95 GPU latency spikes in eu-west during early morning maintenance windows. They last ~30-90s and correlate with kernel updates on a subset of nodes. Paging is drowning the oncall team. :weary:
ria: Can you paste the alert rule? curious how aggressive the threshold is.
mike: Sure — it's firing `p95_gpu_latency > 1.2s` over 5m, grouping by cluster.
alex: That grouping by cluster is the problem, it pages for 1-2 flapping nodes in a 100-node pool. We should group by `node` and require `count>3` to page.
samir: Also we should add a short mute for scheduled kernel rollouts. We already maintain a maintenance calendar for infra; tie alerts to that window if the nodes are flagged.
ria: Proposal: change alert to severity=page only when `sum by(cluster) (gpu_p95_over_threshold)` >= 4 for 5m, else create a ticket. This reduces noise and still surfaces real outages.
jia: Cost angle: paging for noisy non-prod clusters is expensive (pager ops time). Let's make non-prod default to ticket-only unless `impact_score > 0.7`.
mike: SGTM. Quick implementation idea — add a `maintenance_override` label from our calendar job and adjust Prometheus rule to check `maintenance_override == "false"`. If true => suppress paging.
ops-bot: deploy-note: alertrule/gpu_p95_reduced_grouping rolled to staging at 1951234578 by mike.
alex: Example rule snippet I ran locally:
```
- alert: HighGPUp95
  expr: |
    sum by(cluster) ( (gpu_p95_seconds > 1.2) )
    and on(cluster) (cluster_up == 1)
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
  annotations:
    runbook: https://console.redwood/sre/runbooks/gpu_p95
```
ria: For paging we can add a separate rule:
```
- alert: HighGPUp95_Paging
  expr: sum by(cluster) ( (gpu_p95_seconds > 1.2) ) >= 4
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
```
samir: We also need a Grafana SLO dashboard widget that shows p95 spike count vs deployments so oncall can quickly see if it's rollout-related.
jia: Can we add a short quiet window (2m) after a kernel patch annotate event so the alert system ignores the first noisy minute? That will catch churning during reboots.
mike: Yes — our event annotator already posts `kernel_patch_start` and `kernel_patch_end`. Add `unless on() (time() - kernel_patch_start_seconds < 120)` to rule.
ria: One more: for cross-region issues, if only one AZ impacted, don't page. Use `count by(az)` and require >=2 AZs.
alex: Nice. I'll open a PR with the grouped rules + maintenance label check and add test alerts to staging.
samir: I'll schedule a 30m runbook walkthrough with oncall next Tue to sign off.
ops-bot: alert: HighGPUp95 fired in staging at 1951234590 — 2 nodes over threshold (ticket created) :mag_right:
mike: Thanks — we'll iterate. :thumbsup:
